MODEL, SOURCES AND SOFTWARE

What does the model calculate?

The reference run took about five minutes. We ran the original EnergyPLAN engine in a browser and retrieved its result files. The supplied dataset produces model warnings. Using it for energy planning would require further validation.

This workshop runs the original Windows version of EnergyPLAN 16.3 in your browser. Researchers at Aalborg University developed EnergyPLAN to study how different parts of an energy system interact.

EnergyPLAN Lab is an independent, experimental interface. You can find the official EnergyPLAN website under Software and licences below.

Where does the reference scenario come from?

The base model is Aalborg2050.txt from the public HyRES-FBK/moea research repository. The year 2050 is the scenario horizon. The dataset describes a research case and should not be read as a current forecast or an adopted municipal plan.

You can change annual electricity demand (Input_el_demand_Twh), wind capacity (input_RES1_capacity) and solar PV capacity (input_RES3_capacity). The other inputs and hourly profiles come from the base model. A zero in the wind field applies only to the RES1 category. Other wind categories can still supply electricity.

The indicators use EnergyPLAN’s output values and units. The CO₂ card shows CO2-emission (corrected) and lists CO2-emission (total) underneath as the direct model total. Check the scope and corrections before comparing emissions across studies. Costs use the price assumptions in the original dataset.

How to use the workshop

  1. Run the reference scenario.
  2. Change one assumption. For example, increase annual electricity demand by 20%.
  3. Compare the indicators and read the full result file, including any warnings.
  4. Download the input and result files so you can inspect and repeat the run.

The model runs on the device where you open the page. You can use it without an account or a Windows installation. Use Chrome or Firefox. Testing on a physical Mac and in Safari is still pending. Browser emulation can take five minutes or more per run. Keep the tab visible while the model runs. This page keeps scenarios in memory until you close or reload it.

The original dataset refers to a missing profile for additional electricity exports. The export quantity is zero, so the workshop uses the supplied zero.txt for this inactive profile and preserves the modelled energy quantity.

Worked examples

Select Open worked examples to compare two earlier EnergyPLAN runs and download their original input and result files. Each is labelled Precomputed example. Select Run scenario to start a fresh calculation using the values in the form.

Reproducing a run

The program and data come from HyRES-FBK/moea · EnergyPLAN163, commit 5f5df07ebe31d269a8c92832f9f020fe1e5e833a.

9f65cc0e69e5a715b52854fc1aebbfa8a00a6bbfd1118dd348ba293224fc07ae

The workshop reads the result file once EnergyPLAN has finished writing it and the contents are recognisable as EnergyPLAN output. A dash indicates a missing value.

Software and licences

  • EnergyPLAN, developed by Aalborg University. The workshop uses the original executable. Documentation for calling EnergyPLAN externally.
  • Boxedwine build 140 provides the WebAssembly emulator. Matching source code and GPL licence.
  • Wine provides Windows compatibility. Wine 11 source code and LGPL licence. The runtime comes from the Boxedwine Wine 11 web package.
  • coi-serviceworker 0.1.7 enables the browser isolation required by the model engine. MIT licence.
  • fflate 0.8.2 unpacks the program and its data. MIT licence.

Bundled licence texts are available for Boxedwine (GPL) and Wine (LGPL).

Use these scenarios to explore uncertainty and develop research questions. Assess the assumptions and validate the results before drawing planning conclusions.
